title: BATCH-26 FOLD 4: the POSITIVE CONTROL for the H-SKIPWALKIN-1 hand-back, in the HOST'S CLOTHING STORE - the only one of the four player-owned customer shops whose shoppers can leave unpaid at all. Fold 3 measured the gym and the fast food and saw unpaidExits 0 in three runs; THE CODE SAYS WHY (see preconditions), and it is not a rig accident. This scenario makes an unpaid exit happen on purpose, by the same route closing time takes, and asserts the hand-back fires during a skip and does NOT fire in normal play. NO save.
preconditions:
Reporter fixture session fx-hq1 (day 44, MERGED - vars.keepMerger true). Dev build with skipvote / skipstate / shopday / custevict / tilldupes / perf / skippace / enterbuilding / exitbuilding (BAMP_DEV).

WHY THE CLOTHING STORE AND NOT THE FAST FOOD. Customer.Leave is virtual, and FOUR customer types override it to call ForceFinishOrder() FIRST (Customer.cs :363-371: drop every unprocessed entry, then CompleteOrder - i.e. BILL what was processed): FullServiceCustomer :20-24 (the fast food), GymCustomer :56-60, HairdresserCustomer :35, NightclubCustomer :52. In those shops a walk-out is never an unpaid exit - the native code force-bills it on the way out - so H-SKIPWALKIN-1's hole cannot exist there and no positive control can be built there. SelfServiceCustomer does NOT override Leave: it reaches base.Leave, which returns the items to the shelf and sets order.completed with NOTHING added to unprocessedCompletedOrders (Customer.cs :308-312). THE RETAIL SHOP IS THE ONLY ONE OF THE FOUR THAT CAN PRODUCE THE SHOPPER THIS FOLD EXISTS FOR. Of the four t-shopday-pick read, the clothing store at vars.shop ('20 ba:street_fifthavenue', 40 entries for the measured morning) is the retail one, and IT IS THE HOST'S - so the HOST holds its books, runs its live bodies and its till, and is the only machine whose economy figures mean anything here; the client stands inside the same shop and does nothing. This reverses the owner/follower roles of every other t-shopday-* scenario.

The fixture loads at 17:38 with Client1 inside a building, so both step outside for a setup skip to 10:45 the next morning, taken OUTDOORS with no shop occupied (an outdoor skip runs no paper pass for this shop, so it sets no entry aside and cannot contaminate LEG B).

THE LEG ORDER IS DELIBERATELY B-THEN-A, the reverse of the fold brief. LEG B's claim is 'an entry that was NEVER set aside stays a native lost sale'. Once a skip has run with the players standing in the shop, the hourly paper pass has set aside the entry of every body on the floor, and such an entry is owed a hand-back forever after (SkipHandback.HandBack's 'late' path, correctly) - so a LEG B run AFTER a skip could only ever produce a false failure. The negative leg therefore runs first, on a floor no paper pass has ever touched.

THE NEGATIVE ORACLE IS A COUNTER, NOT AN ABSENT LOG LINE: rigrun has no step-scoped absent oracle (oracles_absent is scenario-wide and would fail LEG A, which MUST print the line). `shopday reset` zeroes SkipHandback's counters (ShopDayMeter.Reset :82), so 'handBacks=0 after a 20 s window' is the same assertion, read from the mod's own count instead of from a log scan.

THE MEASURED SKIP IS 6 GAME HOURS, not the 3 the fold brief names. At the shipped rate 50 a 3-hour skip is over in ~3.6 real seconds and the rig cannot place a command inside it reliably (file-drop poll 0.5 s + result poll 0.5 s), yet 'custevict WHILE skipActive=True' is the whole of LEG A. Six hours buys ~7.2 real seconds and still lands at 16:45 - far from closing time and far from the midnight day roll that emptied the till in the fold-3 attempt. NOTHING IS SAVED. ORACLE NOTE: the NullReferenceException oracle carries the `(?<!swallowed )` lookbehind because fx-hq1 prints the mod's own '[Gley] swallowed NullReferenceException' traffic-collider diagnostic, which has nothing to do with this fold.
